transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-29 15:00 UTC | 55m | Arbora Diagnostics security intake
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood brief), Lena (Arbora Head of IT), Aaron (CTO), Priya (Security Eng), Tom (Platform)

Auto-summary (auto): Customer evaluating options for processing PHI-adjacent lab data; wants to understand which deployment maps to their compliance and ops constraints; also wants to see KMS/HSM options and retention controls.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. Quick round robin?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Lena): Hi, Lena here, head of IT at Arbora.
00:10 Speaker 3 (Aaron): Aaron, CTO. We run most workloads on AWS and have some on-prem for older systems.
00:15 Speaker 4 (Priya): Priya, security. I manage cloud security and compliance.
00:18 Speaker 5 (Tom): Tom, Platform Lead.
00:21 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Diego and I will run through high-level security posture and then get into deployment options - hosted, dedicated reserved pools, private VPC or on-prem. We'll capture your constraints and next steps.

02:02 Diego (Redwood SE): Quick housekeeping: what types of data will you be sending to the model? Is it de-identified, PHI, or a mix?
02:12 Priya: Mostly PHI-adjacent — lab results tied to patient IDs. We have to treat it as sensitive. SOC2 is baseline for procurement but for us ISO-27001 controls are nice to have.
02:22 Aaron: Timeline is about a Q3 pilot, production after security gating. We need to prove we can meet encryption, access controls, and maintain audit trails.

04:45 Maya: Understood. Our typical pathway is: start with Hosted for quick prototyping (you can restrict retention, VPC peering options), then Dedicated if you need reserved predictable throughput, and Private if you require a customer-managed control plane or onsite data residency.
04:59 Priya: Can Hosted meet our encryption/KMS requirements? We need customer-managed keys, not just provider-managed keys.
05:12 Diego: Short answer: Hosted with customer-managed KMS is possible for some customers via our KMS integrations — but for full envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys, Private or Dedicated with VPC and direct KMS integration is stronger. There's nuance: Hosted sometimes has limits on bringing-your-own-HSM.

07:30 Lena: We also have strict SSO rules — SAML + SCIM user provisioning and RBAC that maps to our internal roles. How mature are Redwood's SSO and RBAC controls?
07:45 Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is route/model-level and token-scoped; you can map groups to prod vs dev access. Diego, do you want to add how RBAC works for Dedicated/Private?
07:58 Diego: Sure. In Dedicated/Private we expose more granular RBAC through our private control plane — you can configure per-namespace roles, audit hooks, and integrate with your IdP for MFA enforcement. There have been transcription errors in our previous notes where 'RBAC' got transposed to 'R-back' — sorry, ignore that.

10:20 Priya: Audit logging — how long do you retain audit logs and can we push logs into our SIEM? We need 1 year retention minimum and the ability to forward logs to Splunk.
10:34 Diego: We provide audit logs for API calls, admin actions, and model inference events. For Hosted the retention window is configurable up to X days for the standard tier; enterprise add-ons include longer retention and log export to customer S3 or direct SIEM ingest. Private/Dedicated lets you own the retention entirely. We'll share the exact retention matrix.

13:05 Aaron: Compliance: do you have SOC2 Type II and an ISO 27001 cert?
13:12 Maya: Yes, we are SOC2 Type II—I'll attach the attestation. We don't yet have an ISO cert across the whole company, but we have mapped controls to ISO-27001 and have a workplan. For customers requiring ISO we often provide the control mappings and a gap plan.
13:36 Priya: If you don't have full ISO cert, how do we make sure auditors are satisfied?
13:42 Maya: We usually provide our control matrix, evidence artifacts for SOC2, and offer ATE (architecture & technical evidence) sessions. For customers that must see ISO certification we do provide third-party validated artifacts or Private deployment options where customer controls are fully in their scope.

16:00 Tom: Network connectivity — for Private we assume VPC peering and egress control. How much effort is setup?
16:12 Diego: Typical VPC peering + routing and firewall rules: 2-4 weeks to stand up for a pilot, assuming you own the cross-account roles and we have the necessary CIDR ranges. We usually provide a reference Terraform module. We'll send that link.

18:40 Priya: KMS key rotation and key custody: we rotate keys every 90 days but we also require HSM-backed key custody for certain datasets. Does Redwood allow customers to use BYOK with HSM?
18:55 Maya: For Private deployments yes, you can bring HSM-backed keys and control rotation. For Hosted, we support BYOK via cloud KMS in some regions, but not every HSM vendor is supported — we should map that to your vendor.
19:12 Priya: We use AWS KMS with CloudHSM for the most sensitive keys.
19:18 Diego: That aligns well with our Private pattern — we'll include a sample architecture showing envelope encryption where the model servers never see plaintext and keys are only in your KMS.

22:05 Lena: Data residency — our legal team wants patient data to stay in EU for a subset of customers. Can you pin a region?
22:18 Maya: Yes, you can pin region for Dedicated or Private; Hosted offers region selection but not strict per-customer physical isolation in all cases. For EU residency and contractual guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private.

24:30 Aaron: Cost tradeoffs — we care about latency and cost per inference. Dedicated gives predictable pricing but higher baseline; Hosted is cheaper to start. Any rough numbers or should we get a pilot?
24:43 Diego: We can give ballpark numbers but the best route is a small pilot with sampled traffic to estimate token mix. For latency, we can show 95th p50 metrics on our model variants. We'll propose a 2-week benchmark during the SE deep dive.

27:50 Priya: On audit logs I want to confirm we can capture token-level metadata and admin impersonation events. Also need proof of encryption in transit + at rest and key access logs.
28:05 Diego: Yes to all for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has most of that but some access logs are in our control plane — we can provide log export for SIEM. We'll provide examples of log schema and sample entries.

31:40 Tom: Who signs the BAAs / DPA? Do you sign for Hosted? What about Private?
31:52 Maya: We have standard DPA and BAA templates for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private we have an enterprise DPA that covers the deployment model. We'll share the templates.

34:10 Priya: Any isolated tenancy? We need strict isolation for certain decks of data.
34:20 Diego: Dedicated provides tenant isolation at the GPU pool level. Private provides full control plane isolation. Hosted is multi-tenant but logically separated; we can discuss contractual isolation guarantees.

37:00 Lena: Ok — from a timeline standpoint we want a Q3 pilot with limited production in Q4. We need to lock down whether this is Hosted with extra controls or Dedicated/Private. The procurement team will want clear evidence for SOC2 + KMS integration.
37:20 Maya: Next steps then: I'll send SOC2 attestation, control mapping to ISO, BAA+DPA templates, and a short README for private deployment. Diego will send the VPC reference and log schema. We'll schedule the 90-minute SE deep dive to run a latency/cost pilot.

40:45 Aaron: A couple of quick probing questions — how do you handle rollback/fallback if a model variant is down? We need graceful degradation for patient facing services.
40:58 Diego: We have smart routing with automatic fallback to smaller models or different regions, plus soft timeouts. We'll show the routing policy examples in the SE session.

44:12 Priya: One more: retention policy enforcement — can we enforce per-route retention settings and auto-delete?
44:22 Maya: Yes, per-route retention is supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports configurable retention windows by default (we'll attach the retention matrix). Auto-delete hooks that trigger purge and record deletion can be made part of the enterprise package.

47:00 Speaker (Aaron): I heard something about function calling and structured outputs — will that change audit requirements if we do function calls to our downstream systems?
47:15 Diego: Function-calling is just a structured response; the data flow matters. If function calls include PHI we recommend routing those into your private VPC where we don't log payloads in the control plane. We'll document best practices.

50:00 Maya: Recap: send SOC2 docs, control matrix, DPA/BAA, VPC + KMS reference, log schema, and price ballpark. Schedule SE deep dive (90m) week of 2026-07-12. Customer to confirm stakeholders and share KMS vendor.
50:34 Priya: Sounds good. We'll get docs to you and set availability.
50:40 Lena: Thanks everyone.
50:44 Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up.

Auto-generated action items (end of call): See action_items above.
